_notes: Classifier gate. Every PR the overseer is about to review (after the Dependabot / already-reviewed / CI-pending skips) is sorted into a tier, then each harness runs with that tier's model. Order: 1) per-repo override (repos.json entry "tier": "everyday"|"deep"), 2) deterministic rules below, 3) classifier model (agy read-only) for the in-between PRs, 4) anything that fails or can't be parsed -> default_tier_on_failure. A harness missing from a tier keeps its old behavior (Muse/Antigravity pinned constants in review.py, Cursor/Claude built-in fallbacks in review.py). Fixes reuse the PR's tier (cached per head SHA in reviews/<owner>__<repo>/TIER-PR-N.json). Dependabot triage uses dependabot_tier, no classifier call. enabled=false -> classifier off, everything uses default_tier. Edit freely; bad JSON -> overseer logs a warning and falls back to the pre-tiers behavior.

rules._notes: Globs are case-insensitive fnmatch on the repo-relative path ('*' also crosses '/'; a leading '**/' also matches at the repo root; a pattern with no '/' matches the file name). Evaluation order: deep_labels, deep_globs, manifest major-version bump, large-diff limits -> deep; then all-files-in everyday_globs (<= everyday_globs_max_lines) or small-diff limits -> everyday; otherwise the classifier model decides. Migrations are NOT a deep rule (Joe, 2026-11-13: migrations are safer and can be tier 1): migration paths, *.sql and the `migration` label fall through to the normal flow (everyday if small, otherwise the classifier, which can still pick deep).

human_review._notes: Extra-eyes ping for deep PRs that are REALLY risky or REALLY large. The deep frontier review still runs; in addition, once per PR, the overseer adds `label`, posts one comment starting '**Overseer: needs human review**' that @mentions `mention`, and emails `email_to` (piped to email_command, an RFC 822 message on stdin; default sendmail -t). Fires only when tier=deep AND one of `rules` fires: labels (this block's `labels`), globs (rules.deep_globs unless `globs` is set), major_bump (manifest major-version bump), size (>= min_lines changed lines or >= min_files files). Never for classifier-only or classifier-failure deep, the 800-line/30-file deep rule alone, or Dependabot. Dedup: label present, a prior marker comment by github_login, or reviews/<owner>__<repo>/HUMAN-PR-N.json. Failures are logged, never block the review. enabled=false turns it off; email_to empty -> email step logs and no-ops. hold_merge (default true): in self_review repos a flagged PR (just flagged, label on the PR, or a HUMAN record whose label was never confirmed added) is NOT auto-merged even on APPROVE; log line 'merge held: needs-human-review'. Once the owner removes the label, a later --force re-review merges normally (record gets cleared_at). Email transport: email_transport "smtp" = built-in smtplib sender (smtp_host:smtp_port with STARTTLS, login smtp_user, password read at send time from password_file, which must be mode 600 or tighter; whitespace stripped; never logged). "sendmail" = pipe to email_command. Test: python3 review.py --test-email. channels (default ["email"]): which pings to send — "email", "label" (add the label), "comment" (@mention comment). Email-only since 2026-11-13; an existing label or marker comment still counts as already-flagged. The merge hold is based on the local HUMAN record: release with python3 review.py --release-human-review --repo OWNER/NAME --pr N, then --force re-review. Legacy: removing the label on an already-labeled PR also releases it.
human_review.label: needs-human-review
human_review.label_description: Overseer: flagged for a human second look
